item.description:
November 20, 2026 8:00 PM | From $22.71 adv. Event Details and Tickets Hey everyone we are thrilled to announce that members of @cloudsofdelusionofficial and @sunsofstars are coming together to celebrate the 50th anniversary of The Last Waltz at Pisgah Brewing Company! Inspired by The Band’s legendary farewell concert at San Francisco’s Winterland Ballroom on Thanksgiving Day 1976, our local musicians recreate one of the most celebrated nights in rock history.
Founded in 2005, Pisgah is known for producing some of the most sought after craft ales in Western North Carolina. Pisgah Brewing Company currently operates the new indoor taproom with live music several days a week, plus our outdoor music venue in the summer and fall months with live music frequently on WNC’s premier outdoor music venue, the Pisgah Brewing Outdoor Stage. item.description:
Get Ready To Experience The Fire, Creativity, And Raw Artistry Of Metal In All Its Forms!
FUEGO Metal Fest is a celebration of the incredible artists and metalsmiths who shape, forge, weld, hammer, and transform metal into extraordinary works of art throughout Western North Carolina. From the roar of the forge to the intricate details of handmade jewelry, this festival brings together the region’s metalworking community for an unforgettable showcase of craftsmanship and all things metal. Experience live blacksmithing and forge demonstrations, discover one-of-a-kind jewelry and metal sculptures from talented metalsmiths, and meet the artists behind the work. Whether you’re a seasoned metal head, an art enthusiast, a curious creator, or simply someone who appreciates the beauty of handmade work, there’s something here for you.

item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group If you plan to carpool, add a comment below.
Join me for a hike in Bent Creek. We will start at the Hard Times trailhead and hike about 6 miles. We will stop to see the exhibit in the visitors center in the Arboretum - 20 minutes.
Rating: Moderate Length: 6 - Hardtimes, Arboretum, bigger loop back to cars. If you want to cut it short after the Arboretum, that's fine, too. Surface: Trail/Logging Road Elevation Gain: 400-600 ft Pace: 3.0-3.2 mph Dogs: on leash. Gear: In winter, bring a headlamp or flashlight at night. In the summer, bug spray and water, depending on the heat. Bears: None so far this year, but now is the season for them. Features: We will go into the Arboretum and look at the Trolls exhibit, and any other exhibits that interest us. Cautions: Muddy after rain, with some high grass in summer. item.title: Weekly Critique — Wed Dec 2, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Writers This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.
For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.
Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.
If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.
If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).
Source: AVL Writers

item.title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND — Sat Jan 2, 4:00 PM
item.description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.
Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.
The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.
Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

A post shared by Uncle Paul (@unclepaul.music)

item.title: Envisioning the New Year with Creativity & Vision Board-Making — Thu Jan 7, 12:00 PM
item.description: Envisioning the New Year with Creativity & Vision Board-Making with Catherine Willows Thursday, January 7 | 12 – 4 pm Register Here! A new year opens like a blank canvas, inviting us to awaken our imagination and explore what we wish to create, experience, and welcome into our lives. The first New Moon following Winter Solstice offers a beautiful moment for renewal, fresh perspective, and envisioning new possibilities. As the returning light begins to illuminate the winter landscape, we, too, can begin to see what is ready to emerge. Gathering at the Arboretum, we’ll connect with the rhythms of Nature and the Creative Life Force through guided reflection and intuitive art-making. Eligibility: Assistance is available to residents of Henderson County facing food insecurity.
What to Bring: Valid photo ID and proof of Henderson County residency (like a recent utility bill, lease agreement, or official mail with your current address).
No appointment necessary. You can visit the pantry during regular operating hours. Service is generally provided on a first-come, first-served basis.
